# Collision-Bake Pipeline Map — cart/editor

## Bottom line

The `compileOutlinerCollision` bake is **load-time / resident-push-time only**. It runs in exactly one production call site — `cart/editor/world/livePush.ts:101` — when a placed prop is turned into a resident mesh for the /play world. **No export or save path writes collision to disk.** The design-doc §10 quick win ("every exported model gets a `meshCollision.ts` bake into its package") is **not implemented**; there is no collision field or blob in any package.

---

## 1. Save/export entry points (all in `cart/editor/shell/AppFrame.tsx`) and what they write

Four commit paths, all funnelling through `writeModelArtifacts` + `materializeModelPackage`/`updateManifestPlaceable`:

| Entry point | Trigger | Location |
|---|---|---|
| `saveActiveModelNow` | File→Save, first-atlas gate, close/switch, autosave-after-first-save | `AppFrame.tsx:1394`, calls `materializeModelPackage` `:1414` + `writeModelArtifacts` `:1416` |
| Export command handler | File→Export→Prop / Build Piece / Flora (`export-prop*`, `export-build-piece-*`, `export-flora-*`) | `AppFrame.tsx:2131`; `writeModelArtifacts` `:2175`, `materializeModelPackage`/`updateManifestPlaceable` `:2227`/`:2230` |
| `exportCharacterAs` | File→Export→Player/NPC Model | `AppFrame.tsx:3618`; `writeModelArtifacts` `:3626`, materialize `:3652` |
| Background autosave | dirty materialized model | `AppFrame.tsx:5122` materialize + `:5126` `writeModelArtifacts` |

The store functions:
- `materializeModelPackage` (`modelPackageStore.ts:142`) writes `manifest.json` only.
- `materializePackageArtifacts` (`modelPackageStore.ts:177`) writes `mesh/base.blob`, an imported `mesh/<glb/obj>`, `mesh/editmesh.json`, `atlases/base.png` — called only from `assetCatalog.ts:287`/`:324` (import path).
- `writeModelArtifacts` (`modelPackageStore.ts:618`) is the workhorse: writes `mesh/doc.blob` (via `writeMeshDoc`, `meshDoc.ts:119` → host door `__model_meshdoc_write`), `mesh/base.blob` (`__model_mesh_write`), `mesh/parts.json`, `mesh/painted.blob` + `mesh/painted.json` (paint-space verts + doc stamp), `atlases/base.png`, `atlases/base.paint.json`, `atlases/raster-base.png`, `atlases/layout.stale.json`.

**None of these ever calls `compileOutlinerCollision` or writes any collision bytes.** `meshCollision.ts` is not imported anywhere in the store, `AppFrame.tsx`, `assetCatalog.ts`, `meshDoc.ts`, or `modelPackage.ts`.

## 2. Where collision lives in a package on disk: nowhere

Real packages inspected:
- `props/bookshelf_001/`: `manifest.json`, `mesh/{base.blob, doc.blob, painted.blob, parts.json}`, `atlases/{base.paint.json, base.png, layout.stale.json, raster-base.png}`
- `props/Model_1/`: `manifest.json`, `mesh/{base.blob, doc.blob, parts.json}`, `atlases/layout.stale.json`
- `props/cereal_box_01/`: `manifest.json`, `mesh/{base.blob, doc.blob, painted.blob, painted.json, parts.json}`, `atlases/{base.paint.json, base.png, raster-base.png}`

Manifests carry `"decompositions": []` and `"data": "-"` — both empty/inert. The manifest type (`modelPackage.ts:42-69`) has **no collision field**; `decompositions: string[]` (`:62`, `types.ts:419`) is a reserved passthrough. The design doc itself confirms these are reserved: `FLOCKBOOK_DESIGN.md:332-334` ("`data` field currently unused; `decompositions` field reserved"). There is no collision blob in `mesh/`.

## 3. Every caller of `compileOutlinerCollision`

- `meshCollision.ts:250` — definition; `:293` internal `compileOutlinerCollisionBoxes` wrapper.
- `meshCollision.test.ts` — tests only.
- **`world/livePush.ts:101`** — the sole production caller, inside `residentMeshFor` (`livePush.ts:88`).

So the bake is **computed on the fly at resident-push time**, never at export. Inputs at `:101`:
```
compileOutlinerCollision(collisionVertices ?? vertices, doc, parts)
```
where `doc = packageMeshDoc(pkg)` (`assetCatalog.ts:44` → reads `mesh/doc.blob`) and `parts = packageMeshDocParts(pkg)` (`assetCatalog.ts:49` → reads `mesh/parts.json`). The result's `.boxes`/`.triangles` are attached to the `ResidentMesh` (`livePush.ts:112-113`, `:124-125`) and encoded into the v10 MESH_PROPS lump (`meshProps.ts:164-190`) that gets pushed to the host, never persisted.

## 4. World placement side — collision is baked live, not read from package

The loader is `pushResidentMeshes` (`livePush.ts:309`): for each authored placed piece it resolves the package dir, pulls current geometry (`authoredMeshData`) and painted form, then calls `residentMeshFor` (`:341`) which runs the bake at `:101` and encodes it via `encodeResidentMeshes` (`meshProps.ts:79`). The prop's collision **comes from the live bake over doc.blob + parts.json**, not from any stored collision.

Note the door sub-path (`livePush.ts:141-163`): doors bypass `compileOutlinerCollision` and instead get `collisionBoxes` from `compileDoorMesh` (`:162`) — also computed live, and ships **boxes only, no triangles**.

## 5. `pieceShapes.ts` — unrelated to model-package collision

`world/pieceShapes.ts` is the "editor-owned piece decomposition" (`:1`): it turns a catalog-based **build piece** (walls, windows, ramps, roofs, elevators) into a set of `VisualBox`/`VisualRamp` visual shapes for the live overlay (`pieceVisualShapes`, `:135`). It is purely visual geometry for catalog primitives — it does **not** touch `compileOutlinerCollision`, model packages, `doc.blob`, or `ResidentMesh` collision. It's the analogue of the old per-kind decomposition, but for the flat catalog piece system, not for authored/exported models. Design-doc §11 lists it as a separate touchpoint (`FLOCKBOOK_DESIGN.md:331`).

## 6. RJMD Outliner + "visible full-resolution ranges" + re-runnability at load

- **RJMD Outliner doc** = `mesh/doc.blob`, the durable model DOCUMENT (`meshDoc.ts:1-23`): magic `RJMD`, versions 1–3, carrying interleaved verts (stride 8), per-triangle `faceGroups`, per-triangle `faceMaterials` (v3), and per-part `[lo,hi)` group ranges. Decoded by `parseMeshDocBytes` (`meshDoc.ts:238`). `mesh/parts.json` (`readMeshDocParts`, `:211`) holds the rank-ordered part metadata including `visible`.
- **"Visible full-resolution ranges"**: the bake iterates every triangle, maps it to its Outliner range via `rangeIndexForGroup`, and **skips ranges whose part is hidden** — `meshCollision.ts:265` (`parts?.[rangeIndex]?.visible === false`). "Full-resolution" refers to the req_3133 design where the rendered mesh may be a quality-decimated/painted form but collision indexes the **full-res source doc**: `residentMeshFor` passes `collisionVertices` (the full-res `currentGeometry`) distinct from the displayed `vertices` (`livePush.ts:96`, `:101`, `:334-344`). The doc keeps full-res geometry by design; painted.blob is the decimated look.
- **Re-runnable at load?** Yes — every saved package retains exactly the bake's inputs: `mesh/doc.blob` (verts + faceGroups + ranges) and `mesh/parts.json` (per-part visibility). That is precisely what `packageMeshDoc`/`packageMeshDocParts` feed into `compileOutlinerCollision` today at load. So moving the bake to export-time would need no new stored inputs; the doc already carries everything. Legacy packages with only `mesh/base.blob` decode as one identity-grouped part (`meshDoc.ts:276-291`), so the bake still produces a whole-mesh decomposition there.

---

## Which export paths skip the bake

**All of them.** None of the four commit paths (`saveActiveModelNow`, the `export-prop*` handler, `exportCharacterAs`, autosave) compute or persist collision. The bake exists only transiently at `pushResidentMeshes` → `residentMeshFor` → `livePush.ts:101`, recomputed on every live push and thrown into the host lump. Consequences:
- A package on disk never carries collision; anything consuming the package without going through `livePush` (e.g. another machine loading the folder, or any future host that reads the package directly) gets **zero collision**.
- The door path additionally skips triangles even at load (boxes only, `livePush.ts:162`).

## What's available to run the bake at export time (if you implement §10)

At any save/export call site in `AppFrame.tsx`, immediately after `writeModelArtifacts` lands `doc.blob` + `parts.json`, the same inputs `livePush.ts:101` uses are already resolvable: `packageMeshDoc(pkg)` + `packageMeshDocParts(pkg)` + full-res vertices (`modelPackageMeshData(pkg)` / `authoredMeshData`). Calling `compileOutlinerCollision(vertices, doc, parts)` there and writing `.boxes`/`.triangles` into a new package file (e.g. `mesh/collision.blob`) — plus a manifest field (the reserved `decompositions` slot, `modelPackage.ts:62`) — would satisfy the design goal, and `livePush`/`residentMeshFor` could then read it instead of re-baking.</result>
